questions.question: What is the role of finance in organizing a sports enterprise?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Finance plays an important role in organizing a sports enterprise by providing funds for
  • infrastructure, equipment, staff salaries, training, competitions, and maintenance. It helps in
  • budgeting, controlling expenses, and ensuring the smooth functioning and growth of the
  • sports organization. Finance is also known as the bloodline of an organisation.
  • Planning: Helps plan future income and expenditure.
  • Helps cover fixed costs.
  • Preparing cash budgets to estimate future cash needs.
  • Cost control: Helps control and reduce costs.
  • Difficult to set standards: Accurate standards can be difficult to establish.
questions.final_answer: Difficult to set standards: Accurate standards can be difficult to establish

questions.question: What is meant by Debit and Credit?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: In accounting, a debit is an entry on the left side of an account ledger, and a credit is an
  • entry on the right side.
  • Every business transaction uses double-entry bookkeeping, meaning every entry must have
  • an equal and opposite credit for every debit so the books always balance.
  • Rules for Debit and Credit
  • a. Personal Accounts: Debit the receiver, credit the giver.
  • b. Real Accounts: Debit what comes in, credit what goes out.
  • c. Nominal Accounts: Debit all expenses and losses, and credit all incomes and gains
  • Cost control: Reduces unnecessary expenses.
  • Helps determine profit.
  • Monitoring cash receipts and payments regularly.
  • Performance evaluation: Helps measure the efficiency of employees and
  • departments.
  • Time-consuming: Setting and revising standards requires time and effort.
questions.final_answer: Option Personal Accounts: Debit the receiver, credit the giver.

questions.question: In a shoe manufacturing company, the cost material is Rs. 100 per unit. Stitching charges -50 per unit. The fixed overhead cost amounts to Rs 3,000. Draw a Break even chart and ascertain break-even point if on shoe is sold for Rs 200.
questions.solution_html:
• In a shoe manufacturing company, the cost material is Rs. 100 per unit. Stitching
  • charges -50 per unit. The fixed overhead cost amounts to Rs 3,000. Draw a Break-even
  • chart and ascertain break-even point if on shoe is sold for Rs 200.
  • Ans: Given
  • • Material cost per unit = ₹100
  • • Stitching charges per unit = ₹50
  • • Fixed overheads = ₹3,000
  • • Selling price per unit = ₹200
  • Step 1: Calculate Variable Cost
  • Variable cost per unit = Material cost + Stitching charges
  • = ₹100 + ₹50 = ₹150
  • Step 2: Calculate Contribution
  • Contribution per unit = Selling price - Variable cost
  • = ₹200 - ₹150
  • = ₹50
  • Step 3: Calculate Break-Even Point
  • Break-even point in units = Fixed Cost ÷ Contribution per unit
  • = ₹3,000 ÷ ₹50
  • = 60 units
  • Step 4: Calculate Break-Even Sales
  • Break-even sales = 60 × ₹200 = ₹12,000
  • Answer
  • • Break-even point = 60 shoes
  • • Break-even sales = ₹12,000
  • At this point, total revenue equals total cost, so there is neither profit nor loss.
  • Step 5: Break-Even Chart (data for drawing)
  • Draw the chart with the number of shoes on the X-axis and cost/revenue in rupees on the Y
  • axis.
  • Shoes sold Sales Revenue Total Cost
  • (₹) (₹)
  • 0 0 3,000
  • 20 4,000 6,000
  • 40 8,000 9,000
  • 60 12,000 12,000
  • 80 16,000 15,000
  • 100 20,000 18,000
  • Break-Even Chart
  • 25000
  • Total revenue
  • 20000
  • Total Cost
  • 15000
  • 12,000
  • 10000
  • 5000
  • 00 20 40 60 80 100
  • 0
  • 1 2 3 4 5 6
  • Shoes sold Sales Revenue (₹) Total Cost (₹)
questions.final_answer: Shoes sold Sales Revenue (₹) Total Cost (₹)

questions.question: In a shoe manufacturing company, the cost material is Rs. 100 per unit. Stitching charges -50 per unit. The fixed overhead cost amounts to Rs 3,000. Draw a Break even chart and ascertain break-even point if on shoe is sold for Rs 200.
questions.solution_html:
• In a shoe manufacturing company, the cost material is Rs. 100 per unit. Stitching
  • charges -50 per unit. The fixed overhead cost amounts to Rs 3,000. Draw a Break-even
  • chart and ascertain break-even point if on shoe is sold for Rs 200.
  • Ans: Given
  • • Material cost per unit = ₹100
  • • Stitching charges per unit = ₹50
  • • Fixed overheads = ₹3,000
  • • Selling price per unit = ₹200
  • Step 1: Calculate Variable Cost
  • Variable cost per unit = Material cost + Stitching charges
  • = ₹100 + ₹50 = ₹150
  • Step 2: Calculate Contribution
  • Contribution per unit = Selling price - Variable cost
  • = ₹200 - ₹150
  • = ₹50
  • Step 3: Calculate Break-Even Point
  • Break-even point in units = Fixed Cost ÷ Contribution per unit
  • = ₹3,000 ÷ ₹50
  • = 60 units
  • Step 4: Calculate Break-Even Sales
  • Break-even sales = 60 × ₹200 = ₹12,000
  • Answer
  • • Break-even point = 60 shoes
  • • Break-even sales = ₹12,000
  • At this point, total revenue equals total cost, so there is neither profit nor loss.
  • Step 5: Break-Even Chart (data for drawing)
  • Draw the chart with the number of shoes on the X-axis and cost/revenue in rupees on the Y
  • axis.
